research_question: Does Atari Breakout need a trained DQN policy, or can an explainable pixel tracker plus predictive control make the same decisions more cheaply?

claim_policy.verified: Checked against an artifact in this repository or a deterministic command that can be rerun here.
claim_policy.historical_reported: Reported in a merged PR, closed issue, or archived article; the raw run output is not in main.
claim_policy.missing_raw_artifacts: A result is described, but the raw episodes, logs, or weights needed to audit it are not available in this checkout.
claim_policy.not_yet_evaluated: No completed evaluation exists for this claim.

headline.statement: No verified full clear has been recorded under the audited 864-point ALE Breakout detector.
headline.scope: Repository issues, merged pull requests, archived articles, and the completion audit reviewed through 2026-10-28.
headline.clear_definition: Destroy both brick walls in ALE/Breakout-v5, one-player Game 1; the audited detector uses the documented 864-point maximum plus the ROM scoreboard in ALE RAM.
headline.positive_detector_validation: A synthetic RAM/reward fixture reaches 864. A naturally completed ALE trajectory has not been observed.

comparisons.title: DQN (v2) vs RGB predictive controller (v3)
comparisons.left: Dueling Double DQN, Contract v2, 30.933 holdout mean
comparisons.right: Deterministic RGB controller, Contract v3, 137.47 mean
comparisons.reason: Contract v2 makes one decision per four emulator frames; v3 makes one per emulator frame. The evaluation seed roles and episode sets also differ. The raw scores are descriptive, not a fair ranking or a method win.

comparisons.title: Laya Vision vs DQN under v2
comparisons.left: Frozen Laya Vision, no complete episode
comparisons.reason: No complete matched Laya evaluation exists. A 320-frame control diagnostic is not an episode and cannot be compared with a 15-episode holdout.

comparisons.title: Reward shaping vs baseline
comparisons.reason: Same Contract v2 and paired 50-seed evaluation, but only three training seeds. The 95% interval includes zero and the promotion gate did not pass.

comparisons.title: PER vs Uniform replay
comparisons.reason: Three training seeds and 15 episodes per seed. The +0.67 point estimate is not statistical superiority; PER also cost 1.26x training time.

comparisons.title: Contract v2 vs Contract v3
comparisons.reason: Both use the same 108,000 ALE episode-frame limit, sticky actions, FIRE handling, and 15 seeds, but the decision cadence changes the control problem and the meaning of an agent step.

experiments.title: Life-loss observation-window audit
experiments.headline: No verified clear. 15/15 life-loss windows captured; 12,511 ALE frames used.
experiments.notes: Observational sample; no causal failure attribution.

experiments.method: Q-margin, pixel alignment, grayscale range, replay consistency, ROI reachability, detector audit

experiments.title: Laya Vision side experiment
experiments.method: Frozen 201M SmolVLM-based vision decision model, FP32 CUDA, one RGB image per decision
experiments.contract: v2 primary; v3 optional and separate
experiments.seed_summary: no complete seeded evaluation; 3-seed x 80-decision control diagnostic only
experiments.headline: Warm latency p50 72.56 ms; optimized proxy p50 68.36-69.48 ms; immediate reversals 76 -> 10 in the control diagnostic. No complete episode or score.
experiments.notes: Pretrained on some Breakout expert data; not zero-shot. Weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and are not in the repo. PR #74 is draft.

experiments.title: ONNX export and browser deployment
experiments.method: PyTorch to ONNX; ONNX Runtime Web; ALE WASM
experiments.seed_summary: 60 fixed probe states for parity; gameplay is interactive
experiments.headline: 60/60 fixture actions match; max Q difference 0.0; runtime model SHA is pinned. No 50-episode browser score is committed.
experiments.notes: Parity and artifact integrity are verified; gameplay quality is not.

experiments.title: Laya Vision live browser session
experiments.method: Frozen Laya Vision checkpoint served by the local CUDA HTTP bridge; Chrome on Windows runs the dual-game page with the Decision Model controller
experiments.contract: v2 (frame skip 4, wrapper-owned FIRE); interactive session, not the formal evaluator
experiments.seed_summary: contract v2 seed 101; two interactive sessions, each played to game over
experiments.headline: Score 4 with lives 0 after 22.7 s; decision interval p50 67.0 ms with 50-51 ms of model inference; 58.5 presented frames/s; GPU p50 72.5-75.0% at 989 MiB.
experiments.notes: Weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and are not in the repository. The checkpoint was pretrained on game frames that include Breakout, so this is not zero-shot. Controller switching and pause/resume produced no JavaScript errors.

non_claims: No verified full clear, solved game, stable clear, or world record.
No claim that the RGB controller is a fair winner over DQN; v2 and v3 are not directly comparable.
No claim that reward shaping or PER produced a stable improvement.
No claim that Laya Vision is zero-shot or that its latency implies gameplay quality.
No claim that the UI difficulty label 'Unbeatable' is an experimental result.
No claim that a 50-episode browser evaluation or a complete Laya episode was run in this closeout.
